center.title: Notifications
center.unavailable: Notifications are not available on this server.
center.cappedHint: The latest {{count}} messages are listed here; older ones are not shown.
center.noneHere: Nothing here – change the filter to see more.

assigned.label: Decision
assigned.info: A run waits for a decision you may take

failed.label: Run failed
failed.info: A run you started (or a scheduled run you own) failed

failed.label: Check failed
failed.info: A check failed in a run you started or a process you own

resolved.label: Check passes again
resolved.info: A check of a scheduled run passes again after it failed (when the schedule asks for it)

stale.label: Stale data
stale.info: Dashboard data you feed is older than its freshness limit

skipped.label: Schedule skipped
skipped.info: A schedule you own was skipped (missing rights, still running …)

status.label: Monitor status
status.info: A monitor you own or subscribed to changed its status (root causes only)

state.label: Monitor state
state.info: A monitor with states changed its state, e.g. Running → Off (information, when its notification output asks for it)

due.label: Credential due
due.info: A credential you own expires or needs rotating or a review soon (or is overdue)

ready.label: Report ready
ready.info: A scheduled report you receive was generated

unchecked.label: Ticket not checked
unchecked.info: An open ticket reference you are responsible for was not checked for a while

daily.label: Daily summary
daily.info: The daily summary of people who turned it on in their profile (in-app and e-mail only)

undocumented.label: Undocumented access
undocumented.info: The access reconciliation found access changes without an access change entry

share_expiring.label: Share ends soon
share_expiring.info: A share of an item you manage ends in 7 days (it is removed then unless someone extends it)

review.label: Document review due
review.info: A living document you review is due for its periodic review soon (or is overdue)

emergency.label: Emergency access
emergency.info: Someone signed in with emergency access from the server command line (administrators)

due.label: Duty due
due.info: A service duty you are responsible for is due soon and not done yet

missed.label: Duty missed
missed.info: A period of a mandatory or recommended service duty you are responsible for ended without a successful run

exception.label: Duty exception asked for
exception.info: Someone asked to skip a period of a service duty you are responsible for: a second person decides

ended.label: Duty period ended without a run
ended.info: Someone archived or changed a mandatory or recommended duty you are responsible for, and its current period ended without a run

breached.label: Objective below target
breached.info: An availability objective of a service you are responsible for fell below its target (once per breach)

eol.label: Tech stack end of life
eol.info: A component of an application you own reaches the end of life of its release cycle soon (or reached it)

release.label: New major release
release.info: A new major release of a product in the tech stack of an application or system you are responsible for

due.label: Incident review measure
due.info: A measure from an incident review that you own is due soon or overdue

action_due.label: Corrective action
action_due.info: An action of a corrective action finding that you own is due soon or overdue

announced.label: Maintenance
announced.info: Maintenance of something you are responsible for or own was planned, starts soon, started or ended

failed.label: Backup failed
failed.info: A backup or the weekly restore test of the backups failed (administrators)

failed.label: Export failed
failed.info: A scheduled export to S3 failed (administrators)

request.label: Request from an AI assistant
request.info: An AI assistant asks to change something on a platform or to start a run, and you decide

failing.label: Platform connection failing
failing.info: The periodic connection test of a platform you manage started failing

budget.label: AI budget
budget.info: An AI token budget reached 80 % or is used up (administrators; the gateway’s managers, the process owner)

budget.label: Cost budget
budget.info: The monthly cost budget of a service, application or team you own reached 80 % or 100 %

booking_due.label: Contract payments not booked
booking_due.info: Contract payments of last month of a service you own have no cost entry yet (off by default: turn it on in your profile)

volume.label: Contract volume
volume.info: A contract volume your service or platform pays runs out, is used up, passes its ceiling or is expected to end well below its committed minimum

price_review_due.label: Prices to review
price_review_due.info: A price book you maintain by hand is due for its review (Mark as checked when its prices are still right)

failed.label: Data contract test failed
failed.info: A test of a data contract your team owns failed (the owning team’s members and channel)

change_proposed.label: Plant change to review
change_proposed.info: Someone proposed a change to the plant registry that you may apply (never the author)

change_decided.label: Plant change decided
change_decided.info: A plant change you wrote was applied, rejected, returned to you or expired (with the reviewer’s comment)

advisory_matched.label: Security advisory affects a site
advisory_matched.info: A new high or critical security advisory affects assets of a site you manage (plant registry)

certificate_expiring.label: Supplier certificate runs out
certificate_expiring.info: A certificate of a supplier you own runs out in 90 or 30 days

notice_due.label: Supplier notice date
notice_due.info: The last day to give notice on a contract of a supplier you own is 90 or 30 days away

approval_waiting.label: Statement of applicability waits
approval_waiting.info: A version of a statement of applicability was submitted and waits for your approval (approvers and administrators)

deprecated.label: Data product deprecated
deprecated.info: A data product or port you consume was deprecated (registered consumers and the owners of products that use it), with its sunset date and successor

elements_missing.label: Data product elements missing
elements_missing.info: A discovery run no longer found elements of a data product you own (once per product and run)

discovery_failed.label: Data product discovery failing
discovery_failed.info: A discovery source of data products that you set up, or on a platform you manage, failed (once until it succeeds again)

access_requested.label: Data product access requested
access_requested.info: Someone asks for access to an output port of a data product you own (or manage), and you decide

access_decided.label: Data product access decided
access_decided.info: Your request for access to a data product’s port was approved or refused

endorsement_review.label: Data product endorsement review
endorsement_review.info: An endorsement of a data product you own or endorsed is due for its review (or a breaking change or a rating below the floor needs one)

access_review_due.label: Data product access review due
access_review_due.info: The periodic access review of a port of a data product you own is due

quiet.title: Quiet hours and digests
quiet.intro: During quiet hours, e-mails wait and arrive together in one message when they end. Nothing is lost, and the app shows everything at once. Emergency access, urgent sources and requests that would expire still reach you.
quiet.notAllowed: An administrator switched quiet hours and digests off for everyone.
quiet.noWindows: No times – only the whole days below are quiet.
quiet.windowHint: An end before the start runs past midnight: Monday 18:00 to 07:30 ends on Tuesday morning.
quiet.gridLabel: Quiet times in the week, Monday to Sunday
quiet.urgentHint: Failed runs and errors of sources marked urgent reach you at once.
quiet.urgentHintChannel: Failed runs and errors of sources marked urgent are posted at once.
quiet.digestsIntro: Collected e-mails arrive as one message in the rhythm you choose.
quiet.digestsOff: Every e-mail arrives at once. Choose a rhythm to collect a group into one message.

groupHints.decisions: Decision steps, AI requests, skipped duties, plant changes to review. A run waits: at most hourly.
groupHints.runs: Failed runs and checks, skipped schedules, stale data, backups, data contracts.
groupHints.monitors: Monitor status, platform connection tests, objectives, maintenance.
groupHints.reminders: Credentials, document reviews, tickets, duties, measures, access changes, decided plant changes, supplier certificates and notice dates.
groupHints.reports: Scheduled reports, end of life and new releases.
groupHints.costs: AI token budgets and cost budgets.
groupHints.dataProducts: Deprecated data products and ports, missing elements, failing discovery.

quiet.resetDone: Quiet hours and digests: the default applies again
quiet.teamDefault: Quiet hours and digests for members
quiet.teamDefaultIntro: Members who have not saved their own settings get these.
quiet.channelIntro: Cards wait during quiet hours and arrive as one card when they end. JSON webhooks are never held.

admin.title: Quiet hours and digests
admin.description: People and channels can hold e-mails and Teams posts at night and collect them in digests. The app always gets everything at once; emergency access always goes out. You see who uses them – never the content.
admin.none: Nobody uses quiet hours or digests yet. Each person sets them in their profile; administrators can set a default for a team.
admin.channelsHeld_one: {{count}} channel message is held right now.
admin.channelsHeld_other: {{count}} channel messages are held right now.

bot.title: Teams bot
bot.intro: People approve decisions inside the Teams card, with the same checks as in Steward. Needs an Entra app, an Azure Bot and inbound HTTPS from Microsoft to the bot listener. Off by default; without it, cards open Steward (docs/TEAMS.md).
bot.listener: The bot listens on port {{port}} at
bot.noListener: No bot listener: set SM_TEAMS_BOT_PORT and restart Steward. Only that port is published to Microsoft.
bot.appIdHint: The application (client) id of the Entra app registration – a GUID.
bot.tenantsHint: Tenant ids (GUIDs) whose people may use the bot.
bot.providerHint: Accounts are recognised only through this Entra provider, by tid + oid – never by name or e-mail.
bot.credentialStored: A credential is stored. Leave the fields empty to keep it.
bot.credentialHint: Steward signs in to Microsoft with it to post and update cards.
bot.channelsHint: For each channel, choose the bot's conversation instead of the webhook. Other messages stay on the webhook.
bot.channelsNone: Install the Teams app in a channel first; it appears here.
bot.installedNone: Nowhere yet. Upload the app package to your tenant and add it to a channel or a chat.
bot.packageNeedsAppId: Save the app id to download the Teams app package.
bot.approvalNeeded: Decisions in Teams also need a second administrator: the assurance policy point “Decide with the Teams bot” is off.
bot.approvalPending: Waiting for a second administrator to approve “Decide with the Teams bot” in the assurance policy. Until then, the bot takes no decisions and posts no cards.
bot.signInDaysHint: A Teams decision needs a Steward sign-in within this many days: roles and teams come from that sign-in. Default 7.

personal.title: Teams (personal)
personal.intro: Messages you choose come to your chat with the Steward app in Microsoft Teams instead of by e-mail – the same text as the e-mail, with links into Steward. Your quiet hours and digests apply there too. Nothing is chosen by default.
personal.connected: Your chat with the Steward app is connected (since {{since}}).
personal.notConnected: No chat yet: in Microsoft Teams, add the Steward app for yourself and send it a short message. Then this card shows the chat.
personal.notLinked: Your account is not linked through the Entra sign-in the Teams bot uses. Sign in to Steward once with Entra ID, then add the Steward app in Teams for yourself.
personal.events: Messages in Teams instead of by e-mail
personal.eventsHint: Only messages that come by e-mail can be chosen. Decisions come to the chat as cards anyway.
personal.notRouted: Not sent by e-mail at the moment – it stays in the app.
personal.nothingOffered: No message can be chosen: none is sent by e-mail on this instance.
personal.fallback: When Teams cannot deliver a message (the app was removed, or Teams is busy for too long), it comes by e-mail once – if you get e-mail notifications.
